properties.name: A discontinued node now SAYS SO to whoever reads it — `scan_nodes` and `get_node` carry a derived `discontinued`, because all four of the existing readers were computations and none was a READ. FOUND BY BEING WRONG IN FRONT OF THE OWNER, 2026-08-12: `cap:content-store` was discontinued 2026-08-09 on Anthony's word (`dec:the-content-store-is-discontinued`, accepted, OBSOLETES drawn correctly) and its code deleted — yet a brief scan returned `{"node_id":"cap:content-store","status":"realized"}` with nothing marking the retirement. A session read that, believed the store was live and missing only a surface, and RECOMMENDED HE BUILD A SURFACE FOR A FEATURE HE HAD PERSONALLY REMOVED THREE DAYS EARLIER. He caught it himself and challenged the diagnosis, which was also wrong: the first explanation blamed `Capability.status` having no terminal value, when the mechanism `dec:idea-discontinued-is-a-first-class-state` settled needs no status at all. THE ACTUAL DEFECT is narrow — `is_discontinued` was `pub(crate)` and every caller was a computation (three capability detectors, consumption, delivery arithmetic, the report). All correct, all silent to a reader. Same class as `get_node` answering a bare `null` for an unknown TYPE: a fact the server HOLDS and declines to give. FIX: `is_discontinued` made `pub`; both read tools decorate every node with `discontinued`, PRESENT AND FALSE on live nodes so "not withdrawn" and "this build does not report withdrawal" cannot share an answer; both served descriptions now say the stored `status` records what was BUILT and does not move on withdrawal, so filtering a list on `status` alone counts things that no longer exist. DERIVED ON EVERY READ, NEVER WRITTEN BACK — so a reader and a detector cannot disagree, and `dec:idea-does-a-capability-need-a-cancelled-state` (open, marked, Anthony's) is not settled by implementation. 8 tests written first, 5 of 5 mutations killed. ONE CLAIM LEFT UNPINNED AND LABELLED AS SUCH: decoration happens before the payload size is measured so the budget stays honest, and reversing those two lines kills no test — catching it needs a graph within ~22 bytes per node of the scan budget. Toolsnaps regenerated: exactly 2 of 149 changed.
